reader.decision: Approve the allowlist in runner/spawn.py (delete DENYLIST, add ALLOWED plus TINKERBOX_* prefix), update docs/plugin-contract.md, and rotate SENTRY_DSN and BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET as well.
reader.decision_reason: My two-name edit would still leak BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET and every future secret. The allowlist fixes the root cause, and the message says it covers the variables the three plugins read.

reconstruction.problem: plugin_env in runner/spawn.py starts from a copy of os.environ and removes only three denylisted names (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, DATABASE_URL, GITHUB_TOKEN). Every other variable from deploy/runner.env reaches plugins. STRIPE_API_KEY was added on 2 October and never denylisted. With debug on, feed-fetch prints its full environment to stderr. A customer pasted that output into a public ticket on 24 October.
reconstruction.what_breaks: STRIPE_API_KEY, SENTRY_DSN and BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET were exposed publicly. Any secret added later leaks the same way. My plan to add only STRIPE_API_KEY and SENTRY_DSN would still leak BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
reconstruction.fix: Replace DENYLIST with ALLOWED = {PATH, HOME, LANG, HTTPS_PROXY}. plugin_env keeps a variable only if its name is in ALLOWED or starts with TINKERBOX_. Add one line to docs/plugin-contract.md. Also rotate SENTRY_DSN and BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET, since only STRIPE_API_KEY was rotated. The alternative is a pattern denylist (_KEY, _SECRET, _TOKEN, _DSN), which is smaller but misses secrets with unusual names.
reconstruction.cost: A future plugin that needs another variable fails until someone adds it to ALLOWED. The message reports that the current plugins csv-clean, pdf-stamp and feed-fetch are covered. The edit is small, and the rotations are extra work.

reader.closing_answer: I approve the allowlist, not the pattern denylist. I also want SENTRY_DSN and BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET rotated.
